summary: Full P0 E2E pass on Feb-2026 auth-pivot Bracket app. 17/17 backend pytest tests pass (auth, projects CRUD with owner isolation, AI flow steps 1-2 with real LLM, share+reject+owner-reply loop, claim flow, logout). Frontend Playwright pass covers /login -> OTP -> onboarding -> /app dashboard -> project create -> /project/{id} -> inline rename (save + cancel) -> logout -> /app redirected back to /login. One real backend bug found: GET /api/auth/me always returns has_password=false because current_user_optional() projects password_hash out of the user doc before public_user() computes the has_password flag.

minor.issue: has_password flag is ALWAYS false. Root cause: auth.current_user_optional projects {'password_hash': 0} when reading the user, then public_user(user) computes has_password = bool(user.get('password_hash')) which is always False. UI relying on this flag (Settings page 'set/change password' state) will be wrong. Fix: either compute has_password directly inside current_user_optional based on the unprojected document, or stop excluding password_hash there and only strip it in public_user.

action_items: FIX: /api/auth/me has_password is always false because password_hash is projected out before public_user() reads it. Either drop the projection in current_user_optional, or compute the flag at the source. This affects the Settings UI and the SetPassword flow detection.
Optionally register pytest.mark.timeout (or install pytest-timeout) — currently emits a harmless PytestUnknownMarkWarning.
critical_code_review_comments: auth.current_user_optional strips password_hash via projection, breaking the has_password contract returned by /auth/me (always false). This is a real production bug, not a test artifact.
server.py is 1120 lines — at the threshold. Future work: split auth, projects, share, export into separate routers.

auth_otp_request leaks no rate-limit info; OTP_RESEND_COOLDOWN_SECONDS constant exists in auth.py but is unused — currently a client can spam /auth/otp/request and each call overwrites the stored OTP, which is exactly how the Playwright test recovered. Consider enforcing the cooldown server-side.
owner_reply_to_client uses _get_owned_project_or_404 (good) AND then re-calls current_user — redundant; current_user is already invoked inside _get_owned_project_or_404.

success_rate.frontend: 100% on the flows exercised (login, onboarding, dashboard, create, inline rename save+cancel, logout+redirect)

test_credentials: None pre-seeded; tests create fresh e2e-{uuid}@example.com accounts each run. OTP_TEST_MODE=1 in /app/backend/.env exposes dev_code from /api/auth/otp/request.
seed_data_creation: Tests create disposable users (e2e-*@example.com) and TEST_-prefixed projects. Claim-flow test inserts orphan projects directly into Mongo. No cleanup teardown was added — recommend running the Mongo cleanup snippet from /app/memory/test_credentials.md between runs.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend regression suite lives at /app/backend/tests/test_auth_pivot.py. Run with: cd /app && python -m pytest backend/tests/test_auth_pivot.py -v. AI flow test (TestAIFlow) hits the real EMERGENT_LLM_KEY and takes ~20-30s. If retesting after the has_password fix, simply flip line 154 assertion back to `is True`. NOT yet tested: ProjectDocument owner-reply UI surface (P1), ProtectedRoute redirect with ?next= preservation (P1), Claim UI (P0 in frontend list) — backend claim endpoint is verified but the /claim React page was not exercised because the test users had no orphan projects.
rca of the issue: has_password=false on /auth/me: in /app/backend/auth.py current_user_optional() runs `db.users.find_one({...}, {'_id': 0, 'password_hash': 0})` which deliberately drops the bcrypt hash. Later, server.py /auth/me hands that doc to public_user() which does `out['has_password'] = bool(user.get('password_hash'))` — but password_hash is no longer present in the doc, so the flag is always False. Reproduction: signup via OTP, POST /auth/password/set, GET /auth/me — has_password is false despite a hash being persisted. Mitigation: either (a) include password_hash in the projection inside current_user_optional and rely on public_user() to strip it before returning to the client, or (b) compute has_password = await db.users.count_documents({'user_id': uid, 'password_hash': {'$ne': ''}}) > 0 and inject it into the returned dict.
